mainTopic: בר קפרא's stories with רבי, בן אלעשה and the כהן גדול's haircut, the רמוצה gourd, and how the wording of a נדר about pot, stewpot or oven food sets its scope
overview: This amud opens with stories about בר קפרא, who was famous for making רבי laugh. First, he turns רבי's promise of wheat into a joke by using a huge tar-coated basket as his measure. Next, he predicts he will drink wine while רבי dances and רבי's wife entertains him. At the wedding of רבי שמעון ברבי, he makes this happen. He asks about the words תועבה, תבל and זימה, knocks down רבי's answers, and gives his own wordplay explanations only after רבי dances for him. רבי's son-in-law בן אלעשה cannot bear to watch and walks out. The גמרא then identifies בן אלעשה as the man who spent his money showing the כהן גדול's special haircut, and it explains what that haircut looked like. Back in the משנה, the רמוצה gourd is shown to be a type of gourd, and רב אשי's view that it is a gourd roasted in embers is refuted. Finally, a new משנה and a ברייתא teach that the exact wording of a נדר about pot, stewpot or oven food decides which foods it forbids.

steps.title: בר קפרא turns a basket into his measuring cup
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא had been allowed to choose any size measure for the forty סאה of wheat. He coats a huge basket with tar, puts it on his head, and asks רבי to measure the wheat with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said he would take any measure he wanted. He took a big basket, coated it with tar, flipped it onto his head, and went to רבי and said: 'Master, please measure out the forty measures of wheat you owe me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a story. בר קפרא uses a giant basket as his 'measure,' so it looks as if רבי owes him a huge amount of wheat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deal let בר קפרא pick the size of the measure, and he takes that literally by choosing an enormous basket. The tar seals the basket so it can hold grain, and wearing it on his head makes the whole scene funny.

keyTerms.meaning: A measure of grain, about one סאה
A basket woven from palm leaves
Tar or pitch, used to seal the basket

phrases.english: that any se'a measure I want, I will take.
He took a large palm basket,
coated it with tar, and turned it upside down on his head,
and went and said to him:
Let the Master measure out for me
the forty se'a of wheat that you owe me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story about the wheat deal that started before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בר קפרא uses a giant tar-coated basket as his chosen measure for the wheat.

steps.title: רבי laughs and protests
steps.stepSummary: רבי laughs and complains that he had warned בר קפרא not to make him laugh.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי laughed. He said to him: 'Didn't I warn you not to make me laugh?'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי bursts out laughing and then objects that בר קפרא broke their agreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole deal depended on בר קפרא not making רבי laugh. Now that רבי has laughed, he argues that בר קפרא has lost his claim to the wheat.

phrases.english: Rebbi laughed.
He said to him:
Didn't I warn you not to make me laugh?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to בר קפרא's basket joke.
steps.kashyaTarget: בר קפרא's claim to the wheat
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wheat was promised only if בר קפרא did not make רבי laugh, and he just did.

steps.title: בר קפרא: I am only collecting my wheat
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא answers that he was not joking. He was only collecting the wheat he was owed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'I'm just taking the wheat you owe me.'
steps.whatsHappening: בר קפרא defends himself with a straight face: he was not trying to be funny, only collecting what was promised.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He claims the basket was just the measure he had chosen, so he never broke the deal. Answering seriously makes the joke even funnier.
steps.whatToRemember: בר קפרא's humor works by taking an agreement completely literally, which keeps him 'innocent' while still making רבי laugh.

phrases.english: He said to him:
I am only taking the wheat that you owe me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי's complaint.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing: the act was collecting a debt, not joking
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בר קפרא broke the deal by making רבי laugh.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was only collecting the promised wheat with the measure he chose.

steps.title: בר קפרא's prediction to רבי's daughter
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא tells רבי's daughter that tomorrow he will drink wine while her father dances and her mother sings.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר קפרא said to רבי's daughter: 'Tomorrow I will drink wine while your father dances and your mother sings.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. בר קפרא makes a bold prediction about how he will be entertained by רבי and his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line sets up the story that follows. Keep it in mind, because the wedding scene will show the prediction coming true.

phrases.english: Bar Kappara said
to Rebbi's daughter:
Tomorrow I will drink wine
while your father dances
and your mother sings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לַהּ בַּר קַפָּרָא לְבַרְתֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about בר קפרא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בר קפרא predicts he will drink wine while רבי dances and רבי's wife sings.

steps.title: Background: בן אלעשה and the wedding invitation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that בן אלעשה was רבי's wealthy son-in-law and that רבי invited him to the wedding of רבי שמעון ברבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן אלעשה was רבי's son-in-law and a very rich man. רבי invited him to the wedding of his son רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to give background and set the scene for the wedding where the story takes place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We learn who the daughter's husband was and that the setting is the wedding feast of רבי's son. This is where בר קפרא's prediction will play out.

phrases.english: Ben Elasa was Rebbi's son-in-law,
and he was a very rich man.
He invited him to the wedding feast
phrases.notes: The text only says 'him.' Here it means רבי invited בן אלעשה.

phrases.english: of Rabbi Shimon, son of Rebbi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives background for the prediction story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The story takes place at the wedding of רבי שמעון ברבי.

steps.title: בר קפרא asks what תועבה means
steps.stepSummary: At the wedding, בר קפרא asks רבי what the word תועבה means, and he refutes every explanation רבי offers.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר קפרא said to רבי: 'What does תועבה mean?' Whatever explanation רבי gave, בר קפרא knocked it down.
steps.whatsHappening: בר קפרא asks רבי a hard question about a word in the תורה and keeps rejecting his answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each time רבי explains the word, בר קפרא shows a problem with it. This puts רבי in a position where he will have to ask בר קפרא for the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Abomination, the word the תורה uses for a forbidden relationship

phrases.english: Bar Kappara said to Rebbi:
What does 'to'eva' mean?
Whatever Rebbi told him,
saying 'this is what to'eva means,'
Bar Kappara refuted it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The wedding scene begins.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word תועבה.

steps.title: בר קפרא sets his conditions: wine and dancing
steps.stepSummary: רבי asks בר קפרא to explain the word himself. בר קפרא first has רבי's wife pour him wine and asks רבי to dance before he will answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: 'You explain it.' He said: 'Let your wife come and pour me a cup.' She came and poured for him. He said to רבי: 'Get up and dance for me, and then I'll tell you.'
steps.whatsHappening: This step sets up the answer. בר קפרא will not explain until he is served wine by רבי's wife and רבי dances for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the prediction from step 4 starts to come true: he drinks wine poured by רבי's wife while רבי dances for him. His tricky questions were a plan to get exactly that scene.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the earlier prediction to רבי's daughter being fulfilled, which ties the stories together.

phrases.english: He said to him: You explain it.
He said to him:
Let your wife come and pour me a cup.
She came and poured for him.
He said to Rebbi:
Get up and dance for me,
so that I will tell you:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי gives up and asks בר קפרא for the answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בר קפרא answers only after he gets wine and רבי dances, which fulfills his prediction.

steps.title: תועבה means 'you stray with it'
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא explains that תועבה is read as תועה אתה בה, 'you are straying with it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the Merciful One is saying: תועבה means 'you are straying with it.'
steps.whatsHappening: בר קפרא finally gives his explanation, splitting the word תועבה into a short phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the letters of תועבה as תועה אתה בה, so the word itself says the person has strayed. The forbidden relationship is described as wandering off from the natural path.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning God speaking in the תורה

phrases.english: This is what the Merciful One says:
'To'eva' means: you are straying with it.
phrases.notes: It's wordplay: the sounds of תועבה are read as תועה אתה בה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the answer that was promised after the dancing.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תועבה is read as תועה אתה בה, 'you stray with it.'

steps.title: Over another cup: what does תבל mean?
steps.stepSummary: Over a second cup, בר קפרא asks what תבל means. רבי tries to explain, and the same thing happens as the first time.
steps.simpleTranslation: At the next cup, he asked: 'What does תבל mean?' רבי answered as he had the first time.
steps.whatsHappening: בר קפרא repeats his trick with another hard word from the תורה, and רבי's explanations again fail to satisfy him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern repeats: a hard question, answers from רבי, and refutations from בר קפרא. This sets up a second round of dancing.

keyTerms.meaning: Perversion, a word the תורה uses for relations with an animal

phrases.english: At another cup,
he said to him: What does 'tevel' mean?
He answered him the way he did the first time.
phrases.notes: Meaning רבי offered explanations and בר קפרא knocked them down again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the same pattern as the תועבה question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word תבל.

steps.title: תבל means 'does it have spice?'
steps.stepSummary: After רבי performs again, בר קפרא explains that תבל is read as תבלין יש בה, 'does it have spice?' In other words, what makes this act any different from all other relations?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: 'Do it for me again, and I'll tell you.' He did. He said: 'It is תבל' means 'does it have spice?' Is this act any different from all other acts of relations?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי dances again, and בר קפרא gives his second wordplay explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads תבל as connected to תבלין, spice, and asks it as a question: does this act have some special 'flavor'? The point is that it is no different from normal relations, so there is no reason to be drawn to something so disgusting.
steps.whatToRemember: בר קפרא explains both words as wordplay: תועבה means 'you stray with it' and תבל means 'does it have spice?' Along the way he makes his prediction come true, with רבי dancing and רבי's wife pouring his wine.
steps.confusionAlert: 'תבלין יש בה' is a question, not a statement. בר קפרא is asking whether the act has any special 'spice' and means that it has none.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עִיבֵיד לִי דְּאוֹמַר לָךְ.
phrases.english: He said to him: Do it for me, so that I will tell you.
phrases.notes: Do the same as before, meaning dance for him again.

phrases.english: He did.
He said to him: 'It is tevel' means:
Does it have spice?
Is this act of relations any different
from all other acts of relations?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the תבל question after another round of dancing.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תבל is read as תבלין יש בה: this act has no special 'spice' compared to other relations.

steps.title: The third word: what does זימה mean?
steps.stepSummary: רבי asks בר קפרא what זימה means. בר קפרא tells him to perform again, just like the first time.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: And what does 'זימה' mean? He answered: Do what you did the first time.
steps.whatsHappening: A third word now comes up: זימה, which the תורה uses for a forbidden relationship. Before answering, בר קפרא demands the same price as before: רבי must perform for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same pattern as תועבה and תבל in steps 7–10. Each time, the explanation only comes after רבי is made to perform. The story keeps building toward the moment someone can no longer stand watching it.

keyTerms.meaning: Lewdness; the תורה's word for the forbidden relationship with a woman and her daughter
The first time; the earlier episode

phrases.english: He said to him: And what is 'zimmah'?
phrases.notes: The word comes from ויקרא 18:17, about a man with a woman and her daughter.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עִיבֵיד כִּי עִנְיָינָא קַדְמָאָה.
phrases.english: He said to him: Do as in the first episode.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third word in the same repeating pattern.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word זימה.

steps.title: זימה means 'which one is she?'
steps.stepSummary: רבי performs, and בר קפרא explains זימה as זו מה היא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He did it, and he said to him: 'This one — what is she?'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי performs again. בר קפרא then explains זימה through a play on its letters: זו מה היא, 'this one, what is she?'
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man married to both a woman and her daughter would be confused about what each one is to him. Each wife is also the other's mother or daughter. The word itself describes that confusion.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This one, what is she?' — the wordplay on זימה

phrases.english: He did so, and he said to him:
This one, what is she?
phrases.notes: Hear the sound: זו־מה־היא sounds like זימה.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲבַד וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ: זוֹ מָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: זימה = זו מה היא: the man cannot tell what each wife is to him.

steps.title: בן אלעשה walks out
steps.stepSummary: בן אלעשה cannot bear to watch, so he and his wife leave the wedding.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן אלעשה could not bear it; he and his wife got up and left from there.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends here. בן אלעשה cannot stand seeing רבי humiliated, so he and his wife get up and leave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the turning point the repeated performances were building toward. בן אלעשה, whom we met in step 5, now becomes the focus, and the גמרא will stop to ask who this person is.

keyTerms.meaning: To bear, to put up with

steps.whatToRemember: The wedding story ends with three words explained (תועבה, תבל, זימה) and בן אלעשה walking out because he would not watch רבי being disgraced.

phrases.english: Ben Elasa could not bear it,
he and his wife got up and left from there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The outcome of the whole performance sequence.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בן אלעשה left in protest at רבי's humiliation.

steps.title: Who was בן אלעשה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where else בן אלעשה is mentioned.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'בן אלעשה'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses the story to ask who this בן אלעשה is. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question means: where else do we hear of him? The answer will place him in a known ברייתא.

phrases.english: What is Ben Elasa?
phrases.notes: He means: where else do we know this man from?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Side question about a person named in step 13.

steps.title: He spent a fortune to show the כהן גדול's haircut
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says בן אלעשה spent his money on a haircut to show what a כהן גדול's haircut looked like.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: בן אלעשה did not spend his money for nothing; rather, he did it to show through it the haircut of a כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. בן אלעשה spent large sums on his hair, and he did it for a purpose: to show people the haircut of a כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא insists that his spending was not wasteful. It served to keep alive the knowledge of how a כהן גדול's hair was cut.

phrases.english: As it was taught: not for nothing
did Ben Elasa spend his money,
but rather to show with it
the haircut of a High Priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: לֹא לְחִנָּם פִּיזֵּר בֶּן אֶלְעָשָׂה אֶת מְעוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He is the בן אלעשה of the ברייתא who spent money to display the כהן גדול's haircut.

steps.title: The פסוק and the ברייתא behind the haircut
steps.stepSummary: The source is the פסוק 'כסום יכסמו את ראשיהם', and a ברייתא says the cut is like a לוליינית.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'They shall surely trim their heads.' It was taught: like a לוליינית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where a special priestly haircut comes from. It quotes a פסוק in יחזקאל and a ברייתא that names the style לוליינית. This sets up the next question: what is a לוליינית?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק tells כהנים to trim their hair in a set way. The ברייתא gives that style a name. The name still needs explaining, so the גמרא asks about it next.

keyTerms.meaning: Name of the special priestly haircut

phrases.english: As it is written: 'They shall surely trim their heads.'
It was taught: like a luleyanit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural source for the haircut mentioned in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That there is a specific haircut for a כהן גדול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יחזקאל 44:20 and a ברייתא naming it לוליינית.

steps.title: לוליינית is a one-of-a-kind haircut
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what לוליינית is, and רב יהודה answers that it is a unique haircut.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'לוליינית'? רב יהודה said: a unique haircut.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the word לוליינית means. רב יהודה says it is a special, one-of-a-kind haircut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This tells us the style was distinctive. It does not yet tell us what it looked like, so the גמרא will ask that next.

phrases.english: What is 'luleyanit'?
Rav Yehuda said: a unique haircut.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the term introduced in step 16.

steps.title: How the haircut looked
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the tip of one row of hair lies next to the roots of the next.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it like? רבא said: the end of this one is next to the root of that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what this haircut actually looked like. רבא describes it: the hair is cut so that the ends of one row lie right at the roots of the next row.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה only said the cut was unique. רבא adds the actual shape. The rows of hair lie neatly end-to-root and do not overlap.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it like? How does it look?

phrases.english: What is it like? Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: רֹאשׁוֹ שֶׁל זֶה בְּצַד עִיקָּרוֹ שֶׁל זֶה.
phrases.english: The end of this one is beside the root of that one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the physical description to רב יהודה's general answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The tip of each row of hair lies at the roots of the next.

steps.title: This is the כהן גדול's haircut
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא closes: this is the haircut of a כהן גדול that בן אלעשה paid for.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is the haircut of a כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ties the explanation back to the ברייתא. This haircut is exactly the כהן גדול's haircut that בן אלעשה spent his money on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This closes the side branch about בן אלעשה. Now we know who he was and what his expensive haircut was.
steps.whatToRemember: בן אלעשה is known for paying to show the כהן גדול's haircut. That haircut, based on 'כסום יכסמו', is a לוליינית: rows of hair cut tip-to-root.

phrases.english: And this is the haircut of a High Priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects רבא's description back to the ברייתא in step 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The לוליינית cut described by רבא is the כהן גדול's haircut that בן אלעשה displayed.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: the רמוצה gourd
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's words 'and the רמוצה gourd'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רמוצה gourd.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the story and goes back to the משנה. It quotes the next item that a person who vowed off cooked food may still eat. This sets up a question about what that item is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, someone who forbade cooked food on himself is still allowed the רמוצה gourd. The גמרא now wants to know exactly what that food is.

phrases.english: And with the remutza gourd.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: return to the משנה after the long story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who vowed off cooked food may eat the רמוצה gourd.

steps.title: What is a רמוצה gourd?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what דלעת הרמוצה means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'the רמוצה gourd'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what this gourd is. Two answers follow in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing what the food is tells us why it does not count as 'cooked' for the vow.

phrases.english: What is 'the remutza gourd'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the term just quoted.

steps.title: שמואל: a gourd from קרקוזא
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says it is a gourd of קרקוזא, which does not cook well.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: a gourd of קרקוזא.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל explains that it is a particular kind of gourd, the gourd of קרקוזא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, the name points to a type of gourd. It is allowed because it is not normally thought of as a cooked food.

phrases.english: Shmuel said: a Karkuzai gourd.
phrases.notes: A kind of gourd known from that place, which doesn't cook well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A specific type of gourd, from קרקוזא.

steps.title: רב אשי: a gourd roasted in hot ashes
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says it is a gourd buried in hot embers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: a gourd buried in hot embers.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different explanation. רמוצה comes from רמץ, hot embers, so it is a gourd cooked by being buried in hot ashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל reads the word as a kind of gourd. רב אשי reads it as a way of preparing a gourd. Roasting in embers is not the 'cooking' the vow was talking about, so the gourd is allowed.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix the two answers. שמואל means a type of gourd. רב אשי means any gourd prepared in a certain way (in embers).

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
A gourd buried in hot embers.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: דַּלַּעַת הַטְּמוּנָה בְּרֶמֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second explanation that differs from שמואל's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A gourd buried and cooked in hot embers (רמץ).

steps.title: רבינא challenges רב אשי from a teaching about mixed plantings
steps.stepSummary: רבינא brings רבי נחמיה's teaching that listing the רמוצה gourd as forbidden כלאים with another gourd shows it is a species, not a way of cooking.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא challenged רב אשי: רבי נחמיה says, an Aramean gourd is the same as the Egyptian gourd. It is a forbidden mixture with the Greek gourd, and it is a forbidden mixture with the רמוצה gourd.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא attacks רב אשי's explanation, which said the רמוצה gourd is one roasted in hot embers. He quotes a teaching about planting different gourds together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כלאים, the ban on planting mixed species, only applies between different kinds of plants. Since the רמוצה gourd is listed as a separate kind for planting, it must be a species of gourd. You cannot plant a 'gourd roasted in embers', so רב אשי's explanation does not fit.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him, usually from a ברייתא or משנה
Forbidden mixtures, here planting two different species together
Greek, meaning the Greek type of gourd

phrases.english: Ravina raised an objection to Rav Ashi:
Rabbi Nechemya says:
An Aramean gourd is the same as the Egyptian gourd,
it is a forbidden mixture with the Greek gourd,
and it is a forbidden mixture with the remutza gourd.
phrases.notes: This is the same רמוצה from our משנה, which רב אשי explained as a gourd roasted in embers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב אשי's definition given in Step 23
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's definition of דלעת הרמוצה as a gourd buried in hot embers
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא about planting lists the רמוצה as a separate species for כלאים, so it must be a type of gourd, not a cooking method.

steps.title: רב אשי's explanation is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares רב אשי's explanation refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules that רבינא's challenge stands and רב אשי's explanation is rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No answer is offered for רב אשי, so his definition falls. That leaves שמואל's view: the רמוצה is a species of gourd, the קרקוזא type that does not cook well.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation, meaning the opinion is rejected
The אמורא whose definition stands after רב אשי is refuted
The gourd species שמואל identified as the רמוצה

steps.whatToRemember: דלעת הרמוצה is a type of gourd that does not cook well, as שמואל said. It is not a gourd prepared in embers.

phrases.english: This is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes that the challenge in Step 24 succeeds
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב אשי's definition is rejected. The רמוצה is a gourd species, which fits שמואל.

steps.title: New משנה: vowing off pot food depends on the exact words
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that a נדר against 'pot food' forbids only boiled dishes, while a נדר against 'whatever goes down into a pot' forbids anything cooked in a pot.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who vows off 'pot food' is forbidden only from boiled food. If he said, 'Whatever goes down into a pot is קונם for me to taste,' he is forbidden from anything made in a pot.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It compares two ways of wording a נדר about food cooked in a pot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מעשה קדרה' (pot food) means food whose main cooking is boiling in a pot, so the נדר is narrow. 'היורד לקדרה' (whatever goes down into a pot) covers anything that was ever in a pot, even if it was finished somewhere else, so the נדר is wide.

keyTerms.meaning: Pot food, a dish whose main cooking is in a pot
A word used in vows meaning 'forbidden to me like a קרבן'

steps.confusionAlert: The two phrases sound almost the same, but they differ in scope. 'מעשה קדרה' is narrow and means only boiled dishes. 'היורד לקדרה' is wide and means anything that went into a pot.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
One who vows off 'pot food'
is forbidden only from boiled food.
If he said: 'Whatever goes down into a pot is konam
that I would taste,'
phrases.notes: He is saying he will not taste any of it.

phrases.english: he is forbidden from anything made in a pot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the gourd discussion closes
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Pot food' forbids only boiled dishes. 'Whatever goes down into a pot' forbids anything cooked in a pot.

steps.title: ברייתא: comparing vows about the pot and the stewpot
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא extends the משנה to the stewpot (אלפס), which was used after the pot, and explains which vows include which foods.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It was taught: One who vows off whatever goes down into a pot is forbidden from what goes into a stewpot, since it already went into a pot before it went into the stewpot. If he vowed off what goes into a stewpot, he may eat what goes into a pot. If he vowed off what is made in a pot, he may eat what is made in a stewpot. If he vowed off what is made in a stewpot, he may eat what is made in a pot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that expands the משנה. It compares vows about a pot with vows about a stewpot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food went into the pot first and was finished in the stewpot. So 'whatever goes down into a pot' also catches stewpot food, but not the other way around. 'Made in' means the main place of cooking, so a 'made in a pot' נדר and a 'made in a stewpot' נדר do not cross over to each other.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught, introducing a ברייתא
A stewpot, used to finish food that was first cooked in a pot
Whatever goes down into a pot, the wide wording
What is made in a pot, food whose main cooking is in a pot

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the basic rule for vows: we follow the plain meaning of the exact words, and the order of cooking can decide what a נדר includes.

phrases.english: Gemara: It was taught:
One who vows off whatever goes down into a pot
is forbidden from what goes down into a stewpot,
since it already went down into a pot
before it goes down into the stewpot.
If he vowed off what goes down into a stewpot,
he is permitted what goes down into a pot.
If he vowed off what is made in a pot,
he is permitted what is made in a stewpot.
If he vowed off what is made in a stewpot,
he is permitted what is made in a pot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the משנה's pot rules to include the stewpot
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A 'goes into a pot' נדר includes stewpot food. A 'goes into a stewpot' נדר does not include pot food. 'Made in' vows cover only the main cooking vessel.

steps.title: ברייתא continues: vowing off oven food
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא applies the same idea to an oven. 'Whatever goes into an oven' means only bread, while 'all oven-made things' means everything baked in an oven.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who vows off whatever goes down into an oven is forbidden only from bread. But if he said, 'Everything made in an oven is forbidden to me,' he is forbidden from everything made in an oven.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a parallel case: a נדר about food from an oven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'whatever goes into an oven' is read narrowly as bread, because bread is the main food baked in an oven. Only the clearly wide wording 'כל מעשה תנור' (all oven-made things) forbids every kind of food baked in an oven.

keyTerms.meaning: Everything made in an oven, the wide wording
Upon me, meaning forbidden to me

steps.whatToRemember: In vows, the exact words decide the scope, and each vessel is judged by how people speak about it. 'היורד לקדרה' covers anything that went into a pot. 'היורד לתנור' covers only bread, the main oven food. Only 'כל מעשה תנור' covers everything baked in an oven.

phrases.english: One who vows off whatever goes down into an oven
is forbidden only from bread.
But if he said: 'Everything made in an oven is forbidden to me,'
he is forbidden from everything made in an oven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a parallel case about an oven
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Whatever goes into an oven' forbids only bread. 'Everything made in an oven' forbids all oven-baked foods.
